units.note: Out of class, not raised as findings: (a) 'victory soon followed upon what has just been said' renders συνεξηκολούθησε τοῖς προειρημένοις, which more naturally means victory followed for 'the aforementioned' (the Romans); (b) 'the Roman commanders' adds 'Roman' to τοὺς ἡγουμένους, which may mean either the commanders or those who prevail. The opening ἀπέβη τὸ τέλος is the tail end of the preceding chapter (a seam, not a lacuna).
Numbers check out: 3 feet, 16/14 cubits, 4, 10, 2 cubits, 5 sarissae.
Numbers check out: sixteen deep, fifth rank, three feet, two phalangites, ten sarissae.
The closing '[...]' marks the sentence break at the chapter boundary (ἐξ ὧν continues as 'ποιοῦσι Ῥωμαῖοι νῦν' in ch. 32). It is a seam, not a lacuna in the Greek.
